testName: Class A Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Bridges usually freeze:

options.text: Only when temperatures drop well below 32 degrees Fahrenheit.

questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before other parts of the road. Drive carefully on bridges when the temperature is near freezing.

questions.question: If there is a fire in your vehicle, you should not:

options.text: Park in an open area away from buildings, trees, brush, and other vehicles.
Call emergency services and tell them where you are.

questions.explanation: If your vehicle catches fire, drive to an open area and stop. Do not go to a service station because the fuel there could catch fire. Call emergency services right away and tell them where you are.

questions.question: When checking a power steering system, you should make sure that:

options.text: The hoses are connected to the battery.

questions.explanation: Check the hoses, pump, and fluid level in the power steering system. Look for leaks and fix them before driving the vehicle.

questions.question: When braking with ABS, you should:
questions.explanation: With an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), brake the same way you would with any other braking system. Do not change your braking technique.

questions.question: When making a tight turn, you should:

options.text: Not use your mirrors because they can distract you.
Use your mirrors, but not too often.

questions.explanation: Always know what is around you. Check your mirrors regularly, especially when merging, changing lanes, turning, or making tight maneuvers.

questions.question: When backing up with a trailer that is turning, you should:

options.text: Do nothing. The vehicle will follow the trailer naturally.
Turn the steering wheel in the opposite direction.
Turn the steering wheel harder in the same direction it is already turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the steering wheel in the opposite direction.
questions.explanation: When backing with a trailer, first turn the steering wheel the opposite way of the turn you want. Once the trailer starts to turn, reverse the steering wheel direction to follow it.

questions.question: Which vehicle does NOT get an exemption from needing a CDL?
questions.explanation: Military vehicles, emergency vehicles, farm equipment, and some recreational vehicles do not need a CDL under certain conditions. A school bus driver must have a CDL.

questions.question: If your engine is on fire, you should:
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine as soon as possible. Do not open the hood unless you have to. Use a fire extinguisher by spraying foam through the radiator or louvers. If you are not sure what to do, wait for firefighters.

questions.question: For cargo loading:

options.text: The driver must load the cargo.
Another person can load it and be responsible for the cargo's safety.
Another person can load it, but the driver is responsible for the cargo's safety.
Only a shipping company employee can load the cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: Another person can load it, but the driver is responsible for the cargo's safety.
questions.explanation: The driver is always responsible for cargo safety, even if someone else loads it.

questions.question: When an engine is running, acceptable oil pressure would be:
questions.explanation: Oil pressure should be between 35 and 75 psi when the engine is running. Do not drive if oil pressure is low, dropping, or uneven.

questions.question: Posted bridge heights:

options.text: Are legally required to be accurate.

questions.explanation: Do not assume posted heights are correct. The road surface may have changed since the sign was posted. Snow or repaving can affect clearance.

questions.question: You should hold the steering wheel:

options.text: With one hand while resting your other hand.
With both hands for a firm grip.
Loosely if you see a bump ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: With both hands for a firm grip.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands on opposite sides of the wheel.

questions.question: A dual air brake system:

options.text: Has one air brake system but two sets of controls.
Has one air brake system for each side of the truck.
Has two brakes on each wheel.
Has two separate air brake systems controlled by one set of controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Has two separate air brake systems controlled by one set of controls.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate systems but uses one set of brake controls. One system controls the rear axle brakes. The other system controls the front axle brakes.

questions.question: While driving, ____ keeps spring brakes from activating.
questions.explanation: Air pressure holds spring brakes in place while driving. If air pressure drops low enough, the springs will activate the brakes.

questions.question: When driving, you should:

options.text: Plan what to do if dangerous situations develop.
Turn your head around instead of using mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan what to do if dangerous situations develop.
questions.explanation: Scan the road for possible hazards. Think ahead about what you will do if hazards become emergencies.

questions.question: During a vehicle control skills test, a look means:

options.text: Getting out and walking to the back of your vehicle to check its position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Getting out and walking to the back of your vehicle to check its position.
questions.explanation: A look is when you open your door, get out, and walk to check where your vehicle is positioned. You may use only one look during straight line backing. You may use up to two looks during other exercises.

questions.question: Steering wheel play of more than ____ makes steering difficult.
questions.explanation: A steering wheel should not have more than 10 degrees of play. This equals about two inches of movement on a 20-inch wheel. More play than this makes steering difficult.

questions.question: Parked delivery trucks are hazardous because:

options.text: Drivers may rush out without looking for other vehicles.
Packages often fall into the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers may rush out without looking for other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Parked delivery or postal trucks are dangerous because the driver may rush into traffic without warning or step out suddenly without checking for other vehicles.

questions.question: How do you check for a leak in hydraulic brakes?

options.text: Pump the brake pedal three times and hold it for five seconds. If the pedal moves, there may be a problem.
Push the brake pedal all the way down and release it. If it does not return to normal, there may be a problem.
Push the brake pedal all the way down and release it. If you hear squeaking, there may be a problem.
Remove the rear wheel and listen for noise when the pedal is pressed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump the brake pedal three times and hold it for five seconds. If the pedal moves, there may be a problem.
questions.explanation: Pump the brake pedal three times, then press firmly for five seconds. The pedal should not move. If it does, there may be a leak or other brake system problem.

questions.question: If the coolant temperature gauge is too high, you should:

options.text: Stop and find out what is wrong.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and find out what is wrong.
questions.explanation: Stop driving as soon as possible if the coolant temperature is too high. There may be a serious problem that could cause engine failure or fire.

questions.question: You need an air brake endorsement to:

options.text: Drive a vehicle with air brakes.
Drive any truck with a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive a vehicle with air brakes.
questions.explanation: You must pass an air brakes test to be licensed to operate a vehicle with air brakes. This includes vehicles with air over hydraulic braking systems.

questions.question: What type of force do emergency brakes use?
questions.explanation: Air brakes have three separate systems: the service brake, the parking brake, and the emergency brake. Both emergency and parking brakes use mechanical force.

questions.question: Do not shift gears based on:

options.text: What other vehicles around you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: What other vehicles around you are doing.
questions.explanation: Shift gears based on your engine's rpm range or your speed. Learn which gear works best at each speed. Do not base your shifting decisions on other vehicles.

questions.question: To get a hazardous materials endorsement, you must complete all of the following except:
questions.explanation: To get a hazardous materials endorsement, you must pass the HazMat knowledge test, pass a Federal Security Threat Assessment, prove you are a U.S. citizen or permanent resident, and complete an FBI fingerprint check and federal criminal background check.

questions.question: Before backing a vehicle where objects may hang over, you should:

options.text: Cut wires or branches out of the way.

questions.explanation: Backing is always risky because you cannot see everything behind you. Before backing into an area, get out of your vehicle and check the path for hazards. Look especially for overhanging objects that are hard to see in mirrors.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, place weight:

options.text: As far to the left as possible.

questions.explanation: Cargo placed high makes a vehicle more likely to tip. Cargo placed low is safer. Always distribute weight as low as possible.

questions.question: Emergency brakes are:

options.text: Only required when transporting hazardous materials.

questions.explanation: All trucks, truck tractors, and buses must have both emergency brakes and parking brakes.

questions.question: What happens if you stay in neutral too long when shifting gears?

options.text: You may have trouble shifting into the next gear.
The vehicle will be hard to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have trouble shifting into the next gear.
questions.explanation: Staying in neutral too long when shifting can make it difficult to move into the next gear.

questions.question: If driving a truck that needs a CDL:

options.text: You do not need to wear a seat belt.
You must wear a seat belt only if carrying more than 500 pounds of cargo.
You must always wear a seat belt.
You must wear a seat belt only when driving a tank trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always wear a seat belt.
questions.explanation: For safety, you must wear your seat belt at all times when operating a commercial vehicle.

questions.question: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS):

options.text: Makes a loud squeaking noise when used.
Helps you keep control while braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps you keep control while braking.
questions.explanation: ABS helps you stay in control when braking. It does not necessarily reduce the distance needed to stop.

questions.question: You may be denied a HazMat endorsement if:

options.text: You are a lawful resident of the United States.
You have given up your United States citizenship.
You have only been convicted of misdemeanors.
You do not have a mental illness.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have given up your United States citizenship.
questions.explanation: You will be denied a HazMat endorsement if you are not a lawful U.S. resident, you give up your U.S. citizenship, you are wanted for or convicted of certain felonies, you have mental health issues or are in a mental institution, or the TSA believes you are a security threat.

questions.question: Distracted driving:

options.text: Only happens when something physically distracts you, not when something takes your attention.
Can happen even if you pre-program your radio before driving.
Can be avoided by eating while you drive.
Can be avoided by not having complex conversations while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be avoided by not having complex conversations while driving.
questions.explanation: To avoid distraction, do not have complex or emotional conversations while driving. Pre-program your radio before you drive and do not eat, drink, or smoke while driving. Mental distractions that take your attention away from driving are as dangerous as physical distractions.

questions.question: While driving downhill, you should brake until you reach a speed that is ____ below your safe speed, then release the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: When driving downhill, brake until your vehicle slows to 5 mph below your safe speed. Then release the brakes and repeat this process.

questions.question: After changing a tire, you should stop after a short distance to:

options.text: Check that the wheel nuts are tight on the new tire.
Check that the tire has enough air pressure.
Confirm that you changed the correct tire.
Check that changing the tire did not damage another tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that the wheel nuts are tight on the new tire.
questions.explanation: After changing a tire, stop after a short distance and check that the wheel nuts are tight.

questions.question: Hanging meat:

options.text: Should never be transported by trailer.
Must be approved by the EPA.

questions.explanation: Hanging meat is an unstable load because it has a high center of gravity and the meat swings, which affects how the driver handles the vehicle. You must drive with care when transporting this cargo.

questions.question: During the pre-trip inspection test, you will be:

options.text: Asked to explain what you know about the pre-trip inspection process.
Watching someone else check your vehicle.
Watching a video about how to inspect a vehicle.
Changing all the tires on your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Asked to explain what you know about the pre-trip inspection process.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you will do a complete inspection of your vehicle. You must explain what you are checking and why you are checking it.

questions.question: A distracted driver:

options.text: Is usually aware of what is happening around them.
Is a good person to follow.

questions.explanation: Distracted driving causes slower perception, delayed decisions, and poor actions. Avoid distracted drivers when you can.

questions.question: If you are not sure your vehicle will fit under a bridge, you should:
questions.explanation: If you cannot tell if your vehicle will fit under a bridge or overhead object, slow down and find an alternate route if possible.

questions.question: When entering a foggy area, you should:

options.text: Stop on the side of the roadway.

questions.explanation: Always slow down before entering fog. Use low beam headlights, do not pass other vehicles, and do not stop on the side of the road. If possible, avoid driving in fog altogether.

questions.question: Hydraulic brakes can fail due to:
questions.explanation: Hydraulic brakes usually fail because of lost pressure. Brakes can also wear out from overuse on long downgrades.

questions.question: During the straight line backing exercise, how many times can you exit the vehicle to check its position?
questions.explanation: During the straight line backing exercise, you can exit your vehicle to check its position only one time.

questions.question: What kind of brakes do most newer heavy-duty trucks use?
questions.explanation: Most newer heavy-duty trucks use dual air brake systems. This means the truck has two separate air brake systems that share one brake control.

questions.question: If you feel tired and yawn frequently, what should you do?

options.text: Pull over and take a nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and take a nap.
questions.explanation: Frequent yawning means you are tired. If you feel tired while driving, stop and sleep. Coffee and other stimulants will wear off and make you more tired later.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver confronts you, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Do not respond to an aggressive driver's angry gestures. Avoid looking at them and do not try to race them.

questions.question: Is emergency equipment in a vehicle required?
questions.explanation: Emergency equipment is required in all vehicles. You should have spare fuses, three red reflective triangles or flares, and one charged fire extinguisher.

questions.question: After you start the engine, what should happen to the warning lights and buzzers?

options.text: Turn off once the vehicle starts moving.

questions.explanation: Warning lights and buzzers should turn off immediately after the engine starts. The charging system, oil, coolant, and ABS lights should all go off.

questions.question: When does alcohol start to affect the body?
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects coordination, reaction time, vision, and judgment. For some people, effects start with the first drink. Do not drive after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: What should you do on slippery roads?

options.text: Speed up and slow down frequently.
Adjust your driving to match weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Adjust your driving to match weather conditions.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, slow down. Your vehicle needs more distance to stop, so increase your following distance and avoid frequent speed changes.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a problem with an exhaust system?

options.text: Exhaust parts rubbing against fuel system parts
Exhaust system parts that are not leaking

questions.correctAnswerText: Exhaust system parts that are not leaking
questions.explanation: Check that exhaust parts are not loose, broken, or missing. Parts must be properly mounted and should not rub against other vehicle parts.

questions.question: Are wheels with welding repairs safe to use?

options.text: Yes, if a professional did the repairs.
Yes, if the repair looks solid.

questions.explanation: Wheels or rims with welding repairs are not safe and should not be used. Replace them before driving.
